sections.h2: Who handles your Mecklenburg property tax
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. Tax Administration sets values and hears appeals. The Tax Collector mails bills and takes payment. Everything lands on one combined bill from the Collector, covering county tax plus the levies of Charlotte, Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Matthews, Mint Hill and Pineville.

If a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer gets the bill and you get a notice from the county. Before you sell, ask the servicer which tax year it has paid so the closing attorney starts with accurate numbers.

Mecklenburg is a large, fast-growing market: 1,233,383 people in mid 2025, with 538,576 housing units. Owners live in 55.1 percent of homes, and the typical owner-occupied home was valued at $406,800 for 2020 to 2024. Because one reappraisal touches so many parcels, the county posts a lot of guidance online, and the steps below pull the seller-relevant parts together.

The yearly pattern is steady. Bills go out in late July, come due September 1, and can be paid with no interest through January 5 (G.S. 105-360 sets that cutoff). From January 6 the bill picks up 2 percent. Each month after that adds 0.75 percent until the balance is cleared.

Yearly rhythm of a Mecklenburg County bill
DateEvent
January 1Value and ownership fixed for the year
Late JulyBills mailed
September 1Payment due
January 5Final day without interest
January 6Interest of 2 percent begins
February onAnother 0.75 percent each month

If you expect to come up short, contact Tax Administration well before December rather than waiting for interest to start.

Four routes exist. A card payment carries a vendor fee, and an e-check carries none.

  • Online at MeckNC.gov/PayTax.
  • By phone at 1-800-994-1026.
  • By post, using the envelope enclosed with the bill.
  • In person at the Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Make checks payable to the Mecklenburg County Tax Collector.

Skip your bank's bill pay if you can. A payment that bounces back cannot have its interest waived, and a bank transfer can take four business days to arrive. Billing questions go to 704-336-7600.

Mecklenburg revalues every four years, twice as often as G.S. 105-286 requires. Commissioners set January 1, 2027 as the value date.

By the fall 2026 update, 428,506 parcels had been through a first review. Median movement was about 15 percent up for houses and about 30 percent up for commercial property. Notices of Value are planned for early 2027, and the county and municipal boards set rates in spring. A higher value need not mean an equal jump in your bill, since the rate can fall.

Begin by pulling your property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov. The county's own example is a home credited with three bathrooms that really has two. Fixing a record before notices mail is far easier than arguing with a number afterward.

Appraisers watch market data and compare property sales when they set new values, so recent sales near your house matter once notices arrive.

File with the Office of Tax Administration for the county's equalization board (BER). In a reappraisal year the window opens only after Notices of Value mail, and each notice prints its own last date. In an ordinary year the cutoff is the Board's adjournment. The county's steps:

  • Sign the Formal Appeal Form and submit it by email, by mail to BER Real Property Appeals, P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at the Woodard Center, Suite 3500.
  • Add evidence at filing or within 45 days.
  • Watch the mail for a hearing letter roughly 30 days ahead.
  • Ask for any continuance within 10 days of that letter.
  • Expect a written ruling inside 30 days. If you still disagree, you can go on to the state commission in Raleigh that hears property tax cases, again within 30 days.

The burden of proving the assessment is too high rests on you. Timing rules for real property appeals appear in G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290.

Cars and business property work differently. For a registered vehicle, the window is 30 days from the due date printed on the combined tax and registration notice, you first try an informal fix by email, and the full tax must be paid before any hearing. Business and individual personal property can be disputed within 30 days after the first notice of value.

The state offers three programs, and you may hold only one. Each is requested on Form AV-9 through the county assessor.

  • Age or disability exclusion: shields at least $25,000, or half of value if larger, for owners 65 and up or permanently disabled with 2026 income at or below $38,800 (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off value, with no age or income test (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: after five years in the home, bills are held to 4 or 5 percent of income, and the overage is deferred until a transfer (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Anyone selling should ask the assessor whether a deferral is on the parcel, since it comes due when the house changes hands.

The tax lien dates to January 1 and carries penalties and interest with it (G.S. 105-355), so it rides along with the property to a buyer. Left alone, it can lead to a court foreclosure.

A fall closing may still leave the seller owing that year's bill. Make sure the settlement statement shows who pays which months, and get a payoff number from the Collector before closing. Deed recording and excise tax belong to the Register of Deeds, on its own page.

Owners with back taxes, an open appeal or a bill they cannot cover can ask for a written cash offer and choose a closing date that fits the tax calendar. Gather your latest bill, any AV-9 you filed and the deed before you talk to a buyer or an attorney.

faqs.q: Which date matters more for Mecklenburg County taxes, September 1 or January 5?
faqs.a: Both. September 1 is the due date, and January 5 is the last day with no interest. After that, 2 percent applies from January 6, followed by 0.75 percent each month.

faqs.q: When can I file an appeal after the 2027 notices go out?
faqs.a: Right away. In a reappraisal year filing opens once Notices of Value are mailed, and the notice states your last date. Attach evidence to the Formal Appeal Form or send it within 45 days.

faqs.q: Is there a walk-in counter for paying a Mecklenburg bill?
faqs.a: Yes, at the Valerie C. Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, Charlotte, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Cash, cards, money orders and checks are taken.

faqs.q: Will a new value mean my bill rises by the same percentage?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Tax equals value times rate, and rates are set in spring after values post. Compare the new rates with your new value before reacting.

faqs.q: Do seniors in Mecklenburg County get any property tax reduction?
faqs.a: They can. An owner 65 or older with income at or below $38,800 for 2026 may claim the state exclusion of $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger. Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor, and note that only one state program may be used.
